pencereler.0-5: This volcano erupted in the middle of World War Two. Lava swallowed whole villages
pencereler.5-12: while Allied troops looked on. March 1944. Vesuvius, the volcano that buried Pompeii, wakes up. Rivers of lava crawl
pencereler.12-20: down its slopes into the towns. Falling ash wrecks dozens of American bombers at a nearby airfield. Families flee, carrying whatever they
pencereler.20-30: can. Two villages are wiped off the map. It was the last time Vesuvius erupted. It is only sleeping.

bulgular: 12-20s: no central mystery or problem is posed

segmentler.metin: Mount Vesuvius wrecked a wartime bomber base.
It took only a new eruption.
So how could a new eruption do this?
The answer is heavy ash fall and lava flows — and it is why ash load is now treated as a structural hazard for roofs and aircraft.
